name: Orientation
html:
Overview

Welcome to the National Writing Project’s SMLC Source-Based Argument course series for 2023-24. This National Writing Project yearlong course is designed to support teachers in the Missouri Show Me Literacies Collaborative. Over the course of the 2023-24 school year, you will examine your own teaching practices, experience high-leverage instructional approaches, and engage with practical and strategic applications for the classroom—all focused on the specific teaching of source-based argument writing.

Add caption for image (optional)

As is the case with all courses in the Teaching Argument Writing community, this course series was developed based on the research and design of NWP’s College, Career, and Community Writer’s Program (C3WP), a program that has been proven to have a statistically significant impact on students’ argument writing in three randomized-control trials.

Beginning in August 2023, this new course series will follow the 2023-24 school year and is designed for classroom teachers in grades 3-12, including academic coaches, support staff, administrators, and professional development providers. It’s perfect for anyone who wants to learn more about argument writing instruction!

What You Will Get:

  • A state-wide community of educators interested in a deep exploration of source-based argument writing.

  • A dedicated Coach/Thinking Partner from the National Writing Project who will support you as you plan for integrating source-based argument writing in your existing curriculum

  • A synchronous virtual launch that will include community building, a course orientation, and an overview of this approach to source-based argument instruction

  • Support for creating new argument writing activities for your students and teaching context

  • Two lesson studies (fall and spring) that will support you in planning for, teaching, and reflecting on the source-based argument instructional resources

  • A synchronous virtual mid-year workshop

  • A digital credential to signify the completion of each section of the course (35 learning hours total)

Coach/Thinking Partner

This course will be facilitated by National Writing Project teacher-leaders who have practical experience in teaching argument writing in their own classrooms, and in providing online professional development for teachers. Your Coach/Thinking Partner will provide you with individualized feedback on your coursework.

Course Schedule

In the beginning of each semester, you are invited to attend a virtual event. In the summer of 2023 you will be given three options for a 2-hour event (August 15th at 4pm CT, 17th at 4pm CT or 19th at 10am CT). In January 2024 the 90 minute event is on January 10th at 4pm CT.

In each semester there will be one course (4 weeks in the fall and 2 weeks in the spring). You will be invited to try out new instructional approaches, discuss and share with other course participants, and reflect on your own teaching practice and experiences. Your Coach/Thinking Partner will be there to support you every step of the way!

Following each course is a lesson study during which you will be invited to try out a lesson sequence in your classroom.

Digital Credentials

As you complete each course in the series, you will earn a digital badge to show your professional growth. All of your successfully completed coursework will be compiled in a digital learning portfolio that you can access on the Participate platform even after the course series is officially finished. Many school districts accept digital credentials as evidence that counts toward continuing education units, so be sure to check with your district.

Making the Most of the Course

Below you will find information about how the course will work, including information about how to use key features in the Participate platform.

Set Up Your Profile

To get started in building our community, you are invited to set up your profile. Your profile features any information you’d like to share about yourself, credentials you earn throughout your professional development journey, courses you are enrolled in and resource collections you own or collaborate on.

To set up your profile, first go to the Teaching Argument Writing Community feed. Then navigate to “profile” in the upper right-hand corner of the community.

From there, click on “Manage Account,” which will give you options to edit your profile and change your profile picture.

The Course Group Dashboard

As soon as you enrolled in this course, you were added to the course group. The course group is your go-to place for all course-related resources, including discussions, announcements, the list of other course participants, and the course itself. You might find it helpful to bookmark the group for the course so that you can navigate to it easily. You can also navigate to the group through the left-hand navigation in your dashboard for the Teaching Argument Writing community.

Clicking on “Groups” will take you to your list of Course Groups, where you will find all the groups you are a member of.

. . .which will take you to the Course Group Dashboard, where you can find everything you need for the course.

Announcements

Throughout the course, your course facilitator(s) will send announcements to remind you about the timeline for the course and any other relevant course information. Note that you will also receive general community announcements from the Teaching Argument Writing community. Be sure to keep an eye out for announcements about the specific course you are participating in. To track this you can either look for the “Posted in” designation at the bottom of the announcement, or navigate to your Course Group Dashboard, as described above, to see announcements specific to this course.

Discussions

Discussion groups are embedded throughout the course to provide a place for you to share and collaborate with other participants. The goal of these discussions is to build a community of learners where you can find ideas, get answers to questions, and get feedback on planning for implementation in your teaching context.

The discussions are the way to share your work in progress and get feedback from your colleagues; it's also a great place to gather ideas and resources from others. Be sure to follow the discussions as you move through the course. The button will look like this:

You may enter the discussion groups through the links provided within the course chapters.

You can also access the discussion groups for the courses through the Course Group Dashboard.

Direct Messages

As mentioned earlier, you will have opportunities to engage with other course participants by commenting, replying, and sharing resources in the course discussions. You can also send messages directly to other course participants, course facilitators, and community members through a direct message. To initiate a direct message, simply click on the message icon at the top of the site and locate the “New message” button. Click this to begin adding participants to your conversation.

You can also initiate a new message with another individual user from their profile or their card within a community by hitting the “message” button by their avatar. Keep in mind that if/when you are sending a direct message, there is no email notification so there is likely to be a delay in responding. NOTE: If you are communicating with your Thinking Partner, we recommend using the mentorship chat described in the next chapter.

Coursework and Credentials

Submitting Coursework

In addition to collaborating with other course participants, you will be supported throughout this course by a dedicated Thinking Partner from the National Writing Project; they will support you as you plan for integrating the ideas from the course into your teaching context. Throughout the course you will see opportunities to submit coursework for feedback from your Thinking Partner. You will typically have the option to copy and paste a link to a document and/or type your response directly in the space provided.

Be sure to hit “Save and Finish” to save your work.

Your work will be available for feedback from your Thinking Partner as soon as you complete the first task within a course. You may reach out to your Thinking Partner at any time while you are working on a course. Once you have completed all tasks within a course and submitted your completed coursework for review, your Thinking Partner will do a final review of your work before awarding a digital credential. Once the credential has been awarded, the discussion box will be locked and neither you nor your mentor will be able to make further comments.

Course Progress

You can track your course progress in the upper right-hand corner of the course.

Once all learning task inputs have been filled, this indicator will display as a check mark, letting you know that the course is ready to be submitted for review.

One final step! Once you have submitted all of your coursework, scroll to the bottom of any chapter in the course and hit “Submit Work for Review.”

Note: Even if the check mark is displaying, you must still submit your work for review.

Thinking Partner Feedback

When you submit coursework, your Thinking Partner will review it and provide feedback for you. You can access this feedback by navigating to your "Saved Coursework" from inside the course.

This will take you to a page where you can see all of your learning products for the course, as well as a place to “Connect with Your Mentor” through the mentorship chat. Your Thinking Partner will use the mentorship chat to provide feedback, ask questions, and offer ideas based on your coursework. Be sure to make the most of this feature! Feel free to respond to your Thinking Partner with further questions, ideas, requests for feedback, etc.

Access Saved Coursework and Course Credentials

Once you have completed all coursework and your Thinking Partner has had time to respond, they will award your credential for the course.

Remember that you can come back at any time to access all the coursework, the mentorship chat history with your Thinking Partner, and the course credential all in one place. Think of it as a sort of a digital portfolio that captures all your learning from the course.

Finally, note that you can also access all of your earned credentials through your profile page.

And you can return to your "digital portfolio" for evidence of what you did to earn the credential directly from the specific credential page.

ORIENTATION MICROCREDENTIAL
